results.title: Exploring 11 Causes of Frustration for Software Developers — Secret Developer site
results.content:
### The 11 Areas Of Frustration

Here are the 11 categories that cause frustration in rank order.

#### Mapping Behavior to Cause

Finding where a bug is called can be frustrating, and poor mental models of the codebase can cause difficulties that take up much of our working life.

> “We have all been there. Spending hours solving a problem and then realizing it has to do with a typo or layout issue or whatever.  
> It's worse in the cases like our codebase. Nobody has touched some of the code since 2017 and the lack of tests is causing me plenty of ire.”

#### Programming Tools

New tools require a learning curve. Sometimes we need to use a new tool and it might be broken or simply not function as expected. [...] > “I knew the problem was other people.

> Even when the problem was me, I knew it must be everyone else.”

### Impacts

#### Psychological Impact

Frustration faced by developers can have long-term impacts. Some might leave software development together which loses the knowledge and talent they have gathered, while others never reach their potential.

### A Natural Part of The Game

It is argued that frustration in software development is a natural part of the work.

> “Software development has and will always be frustrating. It is how we tackle this frustration that matters and how we solve the problem of our staff leaving and performing sub-optimally“

### Solutions

We need to solve this problem. It is how we tackle this problem that matters as it is pertinent.

#### Tools [...] > ”Breaking down problems seems like a good strategy. Unfortunately, when you are using a codebase like ours with mistakes littered around the code, it is really difficult to get things done.

> If people then give you ill-defined tickets to integrate into a nonsensical codebase then you’re in trouble. This happened to me last week.”

#### New Project Adjustment

Working on a new project takes time. You might be unfamiliar with how to accomplish tasks. Configuration might move to haunt you.

> “I once started working in a hard culture. Project setup wasn’t easy and the pressure started to build at the start of the second day.

> Since nobody would help me get setup I couldn’t start work. Then there were questions about why I wasn’t moving tickets to the right.

> I didn’t last long.”

results.title: The Claude Code Feature I Ignored for Months Was the Most Important One
results.content:
DevPit fixes this with a dedicated design-qa step. After the coder finishes, design-qa takes over. It screenshots affected pages at multiple viewports using Playwright, reads the screenshots (Claude is multimodal, it can see images), and audits everything: layout, responsive behavior, typography, accessibility. If something looks wrong, it reports exactly what’s broken, and DevPit loops back to the coder to fix it.

For mobile projects, the same thing works with Maestro and simulator screenshots. iOS Simulator or Android Emulator.

This changed how much I trust the output. Before, I’d have to pull up the browser after every change and eyeball it myself. Now there’s a dedicated agent whose only job is to look at what was built and find visual problems.

## It’s Not Just Claude [...] Sitemap

Sign in

 work in a real terminal. You see every file it reads, every edit it makes, every command it runs. If something looks wrong, you see it happening, not after the fact in a log.

The TUI dashboard makes this even easier. Run `dp` with no arguments and you get an interactive view of all your pipeline runs. Running, passed, failed, with the ability to drill into any run and see step-by-step output.

## Workflows Are Just YAML

The default pipeline (architect, coder, tester, reviewer, design-qa) works great out of the box. But every project is different. DevPit lets you define custom workflows in YAML: [...] ## Follow-ups That Keep Context

After a pipeline finishes, every agent session has been captured. DevPit can resume those sessions for follow-up tasks:

dp pipeline follow "Make the button blue instead of green"
The follow-up runs through the same pipeline but resumes each agent’s conversation, so they remember everything from the first run. No re-explaining, no lost context. The coder knows what it built, the tester knows what it tested, and the follow-up builds on top of that.

Follow-ups queue automatically. If a pipeline is still running, your task waits and runs when it’s idle.

## Multi-Runtime Support

DevPit works with multiple AI CLIs. The `--agent` flag selects the runtime:

```
"task" " "# Claude Code (default) # "task" " " # Gemini CLI # "task" " " # OpenAI Codex # "task" " " # GitHub Copilot #
```
